notes:
Status: Closed-lost to hyperscaler managed endpoints (AWS Bedrock). Key context and timeline:

- 2024-05-03: Lead created after intro call with Ops + Platform (source: inbound form).
- 2024-05-15: Discovery call (Liam Chen, Priya). Heavy emphasis on SLA, multi-region failover, and FIPS/KMS integration.
- 2024-06-02: Sent pricing + dedicated capacity options (drive link above). POC proposed (2-week).
- 2024-06-18 to 2024-07-02: POC run on Redwood Hosted API (small traffic) — engineering validated latency/throughput; Redwood matched 28-50ms p95 for short queries, acceptable.
- 2024-07-21: Security deep-dive with SRE and vendor risk team (Fireflies ff_2024-07-21_5283). Notes: SRE prefers single-pane KMS and dedicated cloud provider IAM for auditability. They flagged our KMS integration as "extra operational overhead" — quote: "We want vendor-managed key lifecycle + native VPC endpoints; reduces our compliance burden."
- 2024-08-05: Procurement review — internal budget reprioritization announced (Q4 freeze window). Sales engaged with cost-savings plan (batching/quantization) but procurement required vendor consolidation.
- 2024-08-22: Final technical eval — Redwood performance OK, RedTeam requested pen-test SLA and on-demand support SLA. Team felt Redwood would require additional custom contract language and longer negotiation.
- 2024-09-10: Copperline informs AE that they will pilot AWS Bedrock for initial rollout to reduce vendor count and leverage existing AWS contracts. Decision rationale: native managed endpoints (Bedrock) offer unified KMS, integrated VPC endpoints, and simpler procurement flow with existing cloud reserved spend.

Decision drivers (as spoken by Platform lead):
- "We already have enterprise AWS credits and want to keep infra consolidated."
- Security: "Less custom integration surface = lower risk and faster timeline to production."
- Procurement: fewer legal addendums, faster contracting with current cloud vendor relationship.

Post-mortem/notes for Redwood:
- Strengths: product matched perf in POC; SE team well-liked (Priya got high marks).
- Primary loss factor: hyperscaler consolidation (procurement + security). Not a product-quality loss.
- Tactical takeaways: formalize cloud-origin story (how Redwood reduces integration burden vs managed endpoints), produce a one-pager mapping Redwood controls to AWS/Azure security primitives, and a templated KMS/Key-wrapping appendix to shorten legal review.

Open items (closed for this opportunity):
- Support asked for hosted pilot credits to keep a warm relationship — granted $25k credit but procurement still moved forward.
- Customer requested a "migration runbook" to move from Bedrock back to Redwood if needed — we left a contact but no firm timeline.

Next steps for AE: mark account closed-lost; set 6-month re-check to review platform consolidation after their Bedrock pilot; add to "hyperscaler-loss" playbook for product & legal to review contract blockers.
